content.text:
I've fixed the failure. All 729 tests now pass in Release, but that run doesn't prove the fix, because the failure only happens now and then.

**Cause:** the test didn't collide with another test, since each test gets its own temp folder. Every save writes a `.tmp` file and then moves it over the real one. Windows refuses that move with "access denied" if another process has the old file open at that moment. That process is usually Defender or the search indexer checking the file written a few milliseconds earlier. Line 197 is the third save in a row to `source.json`, which fits. The same thing can happen to real users running antivirus or a sync client, and in the app it could stop a save from finishing.

**Fix:** I added `Klippy/Services/AtomicFile.cs` with `AtomicFile.Replace(tmp, path)`. It tries the move up to 5 times, waiting 20–80 ms between attempts, and only retries on access-denied and I/O errors. All five places that saved files this way now use it:
- `SnippetStore`
- `ClipHistoryStore`
- `CommandHistory`
- `AppSettings`
- `FileClipBlobStore`

Nothing is committed yet. Want me to commit it on a branch and open a PR?

input.command:
git checkout -b claude/retry-atomic-save && git add -A Klippy/Services && git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Retry the swap step of atomic saves when Windows refuses it

Replacing a file with File.Move(overwrite: true) is refused with "access
denied" while another process (antivirus, the search indexer, a sync client)
briefly holds the old file open. This failed a Release test run on back-to-back
snippet saves and could lose a save in the app. All five write-then-swap saves
now go through AtomicFile.Replace, which retries a few times with a short delay.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

input.command:
gh pr create --base main --title "Retry the swap step of atomic saves when Windows refuses it" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Why
A Release test run failed in `TransferTests.TransferViewModel_ImportPreview_ThenTagFilteredImport` with `UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the path is denied` from `File.Move` in `SnippetStore.Save()`.

Each test has its own temp folder, so this wasn't tests colliding. Windows refuses `File.Move(tmp, path, overwrite: true)` while another process has the old file open. That process is usually antivirus, the search indexer or a sync client checking a file that was written milliseconds earlier. The same thing can happen to users and stop a save from finishing.

## What
- New `AtomicFile.Replace(tmp, path)` in `Klippy/Services/AtomicFile.cs`. It retries the move up to 5 times, waiting 20–80 ms between attempts, and only on `UnauthorizedAccessException` or `IOException`. It rethrows after the last attempt.
- All five write-then-swap saves now use it: `SnippetStore`, `ClipHistoryStore`, `CommandHistory`, `AppSettings` and `FileClipBlobStore`.

## Testing
- `dotnet test Klippy.Tests -c Release`: 729 passed, 0 failed. The original failure is intermittent, so a single passing run doesn't prove the fix.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.text:
I committed the fix on a new branch, `claude/retry-atomic-save`, pushed it, and opened a PR: https://github.com/seankearon/klippy/pull/42

It's one commit: the new `AtomicFile.cs`, plus a one-line change in each of the five files that save this way. The PR description explains the cause and says the passing test run doesn't prove the fix, because the failure only happens now and then.
